title: Risk Assessment: Replace interactive mode with run_agent_task (PipelineMode.CUSTOM) + remove compose / bin/egg / run_claude
summary: Technical risk assessment for a cross-cutting change that (1) ADDS PipelineMode.CUSTOM, the run_agent_task MCP tool, a Pipeline.active_roles field, roster-subset plumbing, and automatic reviewer_contract inclusion when analysis/plan artifacts are supplied; and (2) REMOVES bin/egg, egg_lib.cli.main, egg_lib/compose.py, ensure_compose_services() and ALL its call sites (including exec_in_new_container), run_claude() in sandbox/egg_lib/runtime.py, run_interactive() in sandbox/entrypoint.py, and the --setup/--reset/--compose/--down/--build/--public/--private flag family. gha_exec is relocated to its own module so action/entrypoint.sh keeps working. Overall risk is MEDIUM-HIGH: the architectural contracts line up with existing executor/BRC primitives (ConcurrentPhaseExecutor already accepts a roles override, ApprovalMatrix.is_fully_acked already short-circuits empty reviewer lists), but the change touches orchestrator models/persistence, the GHA entry-point import path, the integration_tests compose fixture, 65+ tests, and ~8 user-facing docs. The biggest concrete risks are: (a) a stranded GHA path if gha_exec's new import is not wired into action/entrypoint.sh in the SAME PR, (b) Pipeline persistence forward/backward compatibility for active_roles and PipelineMode.CUSTOM, (c) reviewer-graph invariants breaking when a producer is selected without its critical reviewer, (d) integration_tests/conftest.py losing its session-scoped compose fallback, (e) Makefile and docs still referencing removed egg --setup / bin/egg-deploy subcommands. All risks have concrete mitigations that fit inside the single-PR Option A cutover; none are blocking.

risks.title: gha_exec import path break after module relocation
risks.impact: GitHub Actions runs of the egg action fail at Step 3 (Python orchestration) — the entire GHA pipeline breaks for every downstream consumer.
risks.description: action/entrypoint.sh:122 hard-codes the import `from egg_lib.cli import gha_exec` (invoked as `python3 -c "from egg_lib.cli import gha_exec; import sys; sys.exit(gha_exec())"`). Decision-3 resolves to removing egg_lib/cli.py entirely and relocating gha_exec to a new module (e.g. sandbox/egg_lib/gha_exec.py). If the shell import line is not updated in lockstep, or if the new module is missing in the sandbox image that ships on GHCR (`ghcr.io/jwbron/egg-sandbox:${IMAGE_TAG}`), every GitHub Action run fails with ImportError. The sandbox Dockerfile must also include the new module in its COPY layer. The risk compounds because image publication and action/entrypoint.sh changes can land on separate commits and the action always pulls the published image tag.

mitigation.strategy: Ship the action/entrypoint.sh import update, the new sandbox/egg_lib/gha_exec.py module, and the cli.py removal in the SAME commit / PR. Add a test that imports the new module path (e.g. a pytest that asserts `from egg_lib.gha_exec import gha_exec` works from a clean venv). Update sandbox/Dockerfile COPY rules if the module path or package layout changes. Pin the action tag used in internal test workflows to a SHA rather than `@latest` during rollout so an in-flight rebuild cannot deploy a half-transitioned image. Add a one-line backward-compat shim in egg_lib/__init__.py if cli.py is kept as an empty module in the first release, OR document in the PR that the action must be re-deployed.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — the fix is mechanical; the risk is just that a single hand-off is missed. A dedicated test for the new import path reduces residual risk to near zero.

risks.review_reason: GHA import breakage is silent until a workflow actually runs; a human must verify action/entrypoint.sh references the new module path and that the sandbox image COPY directives pick up the new file.

risks.title: Pipeline persistence compatibility for active_roles and PipelineMode.CUSTOM
risks.impact: Orchestrator restart cannot deserialize existing .egg-state/pipelines/*.json files that predate the new Pipeline.active_roles field or that were written with the old PipelineMode enum, potentially stalling in-flight pipelines.
risks.description: orchestrator/models.py:488 defines Pipeline as a pydantic v2 BaseModel persisted to .egg-state/pipelines/{id}.json (see state_store.py). The decision-5 resolution adds a new field `active_roles: list[str] | None = Field(default=None)`. Pydantic v2 is strict by default: if model_config does not set `extra='ignore'` / `extra='allow'`, or if active_roles is somehow added as non-Optional in a future iteration, old JSON files that predate the field will deserialize but NEW JSON written by the upgraded orchestrator might be rejected by an OLD orchestrator on rollback. Separately, PipelineMode is a StrEnum (models.py:29) — adding CUSTOM is additive, so old pipelines (mode='issue' | 'babysit') still deserialize, but a new pipeline with mode='custom' serialized by the upgraded orchestrator cannot be loaded by an old orchestrator running against the same state directory (rollback-incompatible). There is no explicit migration step.

mitigation.strategy: Default active_roles to None in the Pydantic field. Explicitly set pydantic `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='ignore')` on Pipeline so unknown fields from either direction are tolerated. Add a state_store unit test that loads a canonical pre-change Pipeline JSON fixture and asserts it round-trips post-change. Document the forward-only compatibility (CUSTOM pipelines require the new orchestrator) in RELEASING.md and CHANGELOG. Add a load-time defensive branch in state_store that coerces `mode` values it doesn't recognize into a safe default (ISSUE) rather than raising, OR fail loud with a clear message instead of silent data loss.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — Pydantic's default-value handling covers the add-field case; the rollback asymmetry is documented rather than eliminated (acceptable for an additive enum variant).

risks.title: Review-graph invariant: producer selected without its critical reviewer causes BRC deadlock
risks.impact: A run_agent_task invocation with an unbalanced roster (e.g. roles=['coder'] without reviewer_code) causes the producer to propose but never reach CONSENSUS_REACHED — the pipeline hangs until timeout.
risks.description: ApprovalMatrix.is_fully_acked (approval_matrix.py:162) short-circuits to True ONLY when `critical_reviewers_for(producer)` returns an EMPTY set. If the review graph still lists reviewer_code as a critical reviewer of coder (because ReviewGraph is built from the unfiltered phase roster), but reviewer_code is NOT in active_roles and therefore never spawned, the for-loop at line 173 iterates over reviewer_code, finds no ApprovalEntry, returns False, and the producer blocks forever. pipelines.py:7263–7270 filters the review graph to the active role set today, but only when roles is explicitly overridden — this path must be exercised and covered by tests. Decision-6 chose 'reject at validation' to force `at least one producer`, but does NOT mandate that each producer's critical reviewers are in the roster. The issue statement says reviewer_contract is auto-included when artifacts are present — the same pattern (auto-include critical reviewers for every chosen producer) is NOT in the resolution and needs an explicit rule.

mitigation.strategy: Add a validation step in the run_agent_task handler (or in ConcurrentPhaseExecutor.__init__) that, for every producer role in active_roles, verifies at least one of its critical_reviewers is also in active_roles OR that critical_reviewers_for(producer) is empty by design. On failure, return HTTP 400 with a clear message: 'Producer <X> requires one of reviewers <Y,Z> but none were selected.' Add an alternative policy (and test) that auto-injects the producer's mandatory critical reviewers — matching the reviewer_contract auto-include pattern in the issue spec. Add a focused test (tests/orchestrator/test_run_agent_task_validation.py) with explicit cases: (a) coder-only → rejected, (b) coder+reviewer_code → allowed, (c) coder+reviewer_code+tester → allowed (tester has no critical reviewer when alone — verify short-circuit). The task_planner should add this as a discrete task.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — an explicit validation rule plus a focused test suite covers the deadlock surface.

risks.review_reason: Decision-6 resolves the trivial degenerate case (reviewer-only roster) but not the non-trivial one (producer without reviewer). This should be an explicit plan-phase decision point so the task_planner captures it as a task with acceptance criteria.

risks.title: integration_tests loses session-scoped compose fallback
risks.impact: Integration test suite (integration_tests/test_e2e_workflow.py, test_babysit_pr/*, test_agent_security_fuzz.py) fails to start — every test that depends on the `egg_stack` fixture errors at fixture setup.
risks.description: integration_tests/conftest.py defines a session-scoped `egg_stack` fixture that launches gateway+orchestrator via docker-compose as a fallback when k8s is unavailable. Decision-4 mandates 'Full cutover — delete compose.py module and ALL call sites, including ensure_compose_services() in exec_in_new_container(). Integration test fixtures should migrate too.' If the compose path is deleted without replacing the fixture's fallback with either a k8s setup or a fixture skip, every integration test fails in local developer environments that don't run k8s. This is a CERTAIN materialization: any contributor running `make test` without k3s/minikube breaks immediately.

mitigation.strategy: Rewrite egg_stack fixture to require k8s (kind/minikube/k3s) and pytest.skip() cleanly when k8s is not reachable, rather than falling back to compose. Update Makefile.test to document the k8s prerequisite. Add a CONTRIBUTING.md section describing how to spin up a dev k8s cluster. Optionally provide a `make test-unit` target that runs only the unit-test subset so contributors without k8s have a path to run SOMETHING locally. The task_planner should add a dedicated 'Migrate integration test fixtures to k8s-only' task with explicit acceptance criteria (clean skip, Makefile docs updated, CONTRIBUTING updated).
mitigation.residual_risk: MEDIUM — even with a clean skip, the developer experience of running integration tests locally degrades until k3s becomes a standard dev dependency. This is tracked risk, not a blocker.

risks.title: Existing PipelineMode.BABYSIT conditional branches don't handle CUSTOM
risks.impact: Logic in pipelines.py, concurrent_executor.py, and state_store.py that checks `mode == PipelineMode.BABYSIT` treats CUSTOM as ISSUE by default — which is sometimes right and sometimes silently wrong (e.g. branch naming, contract filtering).
risks.description: grep confirms BABYSIT-specific branches at orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:353, 754, 768, 822, 825, 957, 959, 6192, 6357, 9661; orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py:174; orchestrator/state_store.py:882. None of these sites explicitly handle a new CUSTOM variant. Critical examples: (a) pipelines.py:957 sets `has_contract = mode != PipelineMode.BABYSIT` — for CUSTOM, has_contract will default to True even when no contract exists (refine-phase custom run with only a refiner). (b) concurrent_executor.py:174 only uses per-role staging branches when mode == BABYSIT; CUSTOM with pr_number (decision-2 chose 'CUSTOM subsumes BABYSIT') will NOT use per-role staging branches unless the check is generalized to `mode in {BABYSIT, CUSTOM}` or dispatched by pr_number presence.

mitigation.strategy: Audit every `mode == PipelineMode.BABYSIT` and `mode != PipelineMode.BABYSIT` site and decide per-site whether CUSTOM should take the ISSUE path, the BABYSIT path, or a third path. The task_planner should add a discrete task 'Audit PipelineMode conditionals for CUSTOM' with the branch list enumerated as acceptance criteria. Where CUSTOM should behave like BABYSIT (e.g. per-role staging branches when pr_number is set), extract a helper `_uses_per_role_staging(pipeline) -> bool` so the policy is centralized. Add unit tests for CUSTOM mode at each site.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — mechanical audit with good test coverage closes this risk. The risk is volume, not difficulty.

risks.review_reason: Decision-2 couples CUSTOM to BABYSIT semantics when pr_number is present; the branch-by-branch call is a policy judgement that should be explicit in the plan rather than decided ad-hoc during implement.

risks.title: `egg` entry point in pyproject.toml points to deleted egg_lib.cli:main
risks.impact: After `pip install -e .` or `uv pip install -e .`, the `egg` shell command errors with ImportError — breaks any developer workflow that invokes `egg ...` directly and breaks the `make ...` targets that reference `egg --setup`.
risks.description: pyproject.toml line 43 registers `egg = "egg_lib.cli:main"` under [project.scripts]. Decision-3 removes egg_lib.cli entirely; the entry point must be removed in the same PR. Makefile:364 and Makefile:369 reference `egg --setup` in user-facing error messages (telling contributors to run it when config is missing) — these messages become misleading after removal. No GHA workflow invokes `egg` directly (action/entrypoint.sh imports the Python function), so the GHA path is unaffected.

mitigation.strategy: Remove the `egg` entry from [project.scripts] in pyproject.toml in the same commit that removes egg_lib/cli.py. Update Makefile:364 and :369 to point to `bin/egg-deploy init` or the new onboarding flow (whatever replaces `--setup`). Audit any `shared/egg_config/` CLI helpers that reference `egg --setup` in docstrings/error text. Add a test that either asserts the script is gone or skips on its absence.

risks.title: sandbox/entrypoint.py `sys.argv == 1` branch dispatches into deleted run_interactive()
risks.impact: If the sandbox container is started without args in non-orchestrator mode (e.g. a dev `docker run` or a stale CI invocation), it errors with AttributeError/NameError instead of a clean exit.
risks.description: sandbox/entrypoint.py:2131–2145 dispatches on sys.argv length: `if len(sys.argv) == 1 and not config.is_orchestrator_mode: run_interactive(config, logger)`. Removing run_interactive() leaves this branch referencing an undefined name. The new world is explicit-args-only, so the branch should either (a) print usage and exit 2, or (b) be deleted along with run_interactive. Tests in sandbox/tests/test_entrypoint_pipeline_guard.py and tests/sandbox/test_entrypoint.py exercise the dispatch path and will fail.

mitigation.strategy: Replace the `run_interactive(config, logger)` call with a clean `logger.error('interactive mode is no longer supported; pass a command'); return 2`. Update tests to assert the new error path. Document the change in the sandbox README so anyone manually running the container understands.

risks.title: bin/egg-deploy compose subcommands silently remain in tree after being stripped
risks.impact: Operators who read bin/egg-deploy --help or trust existing docs invoke removed subcommands and get bash errors instead of a clear 'removed — use kubectl' message.
risks.description: bin/egg-deploy (383 lines) has up/down/status/logs/build/init subcommands. Of these, everything except `init` is compose-based (lines 26, 141, 284, 305, 321, 329). The refine analysis notes the file `docker-compose.yml` has ALREADY been removed from the tree, so the compose subcommands are broken in practice today. Decision-4 removes compose.py and call sites but the scope of bin/egg-deploy cleanup is not explicit in the HITL resolutions. Options: delete the compose subcommands and keep only `init`; delete bin/egg-deploy entirely; or replace the compose subcommands with stubs that print 'deprecated — use kubectl / k8s guide'.

mitigation.strategy: In the same PR, delete the compose subcommands from bin/egg-deploy and replace them with a single dispatch case that prints: 'Compose-based deploy has been removed. See docs/guides/deployment.md for the k8s setup.' Keep `init` if it is still meaningful; delete the script entirely otherwise. Update the Makefile and docs in the same PR. The task_planner should capture this as a discrete task so it is not forgotten.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — clear deprecation messaging + doc updates.

risks.title: Security: run_agent_task `repo` parameter allows arbitrary repo without allowlist enforcement
risks.impact: If the MCP tool accepts any `owner/name` string, a caller with MCP access could spawn k8s Jobs that write/push to repos outside the configured allowlist, potentially leaking credentials or producing unreviewed PRs against repos the operator never intended to touch.
risks.description: The MCP server enforces caller auth via EGG_LAUNCHER_SECRET (orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1598), so random external callers cannot invoke run_agent_task. However, within a trusted session, the `repo` parameter is a free-form string. The repositories allowlist (shared/egg_config/repositories.yaml, enforced via orchestrator/routes/signals.py:844 and pipelines.py:6658 at check-time) is consulted for per-repo check commands but is not obviously enforced at pipeline-creation time. submit_task / babysit_pr presumably do enforce this today — the new tool must inherit the same enforcement, and the task_planner must capture it as an explicit acceptance criterion, not 'implicit via submit_task code reuse'.

mitigation.strategy: Add explicit validation in the run_agent_task handler: look up the repo in shared/egg_config/config.get_repos() (or equivalent) before pipeline creation; reject with 400 if missing. Mirror exactly how submit_task / babysit_pr validate repo. Add a focused security test (tests/orchestrator/test_run_agent_task_security.py) with cases: (a) repo in allowlist → accepted, (b) repo not in allowlist → 400, (c) repo with shell-metacharacters or path-traversal → 400. The task_planner should include this as an explicit task with acceptance criteria pulled verbatim into the contract.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — same pattern as existing tools; straightforward to test.

risks.review_reason: Any new tool that spawns agents with git credentials deserves an explicit security review. The allowlist check is mechanical but the decision to reuse or diverge from submit_task's validation should be conscious.

risks.title: Branch/worktree proliferation for auto-generated `egg/custom-<pipeline_id>` branches
risks.impact: Over time, rapid-fire run_agent_task calls create an accumulation of per-pipeline branches on the remote and per-role worktrees on the gateway node.
risks.description: Decision-7 auto-generates `egg/custom-<pipeline_id>` branches when no branch is passed. Pipeline IDs are UUID-ish, so each CUSTOM run generates a new branch on push. There is no automatic cleanup; over months this accumulates. Worktree directory growth on the gateway (managed by gateway code) is bounded per pipeline but unbounded in aggregate. This is a slow, visible-to-operators problem — not a blocker.

mitigation.strategy: Document the branch naming convention in CHANGELOG / docs so operators know to run `git push origin --delete $(git branch -r --list 'origin/egg/custom-*' | awk -F/ '{print $2"/"$3"/"$4}')` or similar on a schedule. Issue a follow-up ticket for a scheduled cleanup job. For gateway worktrees, confirm the existing cleanup flow (issue #1865 family of fixes) handles CUSTOM pipelines the same as ISSUE/BABYSIT. Add a log line on CUSTOM pipeline completion that prints the branch name so operators can track.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — accepted as a known operational concern with a tracked follow-up.

risks.title: Draft artifact naming collision between CUSTOM and ISSUE pipelines on the same issue_number
risks.impact: A CUSTOM pipeline with issue_number=N could overwrite .egg-state/drafts/N-analysis.md (or -plan.md) belonging to an ISSUE pipeline running in parallel on the same issue.
risks.description: The optional `issue_number` parameter to run_agent_task lets the caller associate a CUSTOM run with an existing issue. Drafts are historically named `.egg-state/drafts/<issue>-analysis.md` / `<issue>-plan.md`. If a CUSTOM run provides both issue_number and `analysis` or `plan` pre-populated content, it could overwrite an in-flight ISSUE pipeline's drafts. feedback-1 Q2 (contract-file keying) is deferred to this phase but not resolved in the HITL section.

mitigation.strategy: For CUSTOM pipelines, always use pipeline_id-keyed draft filenames (`.egg-state/drafts/<pipeline_id>-analysis.md`) regardless of issue_number. issue_number remains an informational field for the contract, not a draft-file key. The task_planner should capture this as an explicit task and resolve feedback-1 Q2 as 'pipeline-keyed for CUSTOM, issue-keyed for ISSUE/BABYSIT'. Add a test for parallel ISSUE+CUSTOM runs against the same issue that asserts no file collision.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — once the naming rule is explicit, collision is impossible.

risks.review_reason: feedback-1 Q2 explicitly defers contract-file keying to this plan phase; the plan must resolve it rather than leave it ambiguous for the coder.

risks.title: Large test churn (65+ tests) and large single-PR diff
risks.impact: PR review is slow; a single missed test update causes a late-stage CI failure that forces a re-push; reviewer fatigue increases the chance of missing a subtle issue.
risks.description: The refine analysis identified affected test files: tests/sandbox/test_cli_main.py (11 tests), integration_tests/conftest.py (session fixture), tests/sandbox/test_entrypoint.py (~30 tests), integration_tests/test_e2e_workflow.py (~10 tests), sandbox/tests/test_entrypoint_pipeline_guard.py (~5 tests). Adding the new tool surface needs its own test coverage (route validation, roster filtering, reviewer auto-include, security allowlist — 20+ new tests). Total churn: ~65+ tests affected + ~25 new tests. This is not a risk in the correctness sense but a rollout risk.

mitigation.strategy: The task_planner should decompose the PR into clearly-named commits: 'add PipelineMode.CUSTOM + active_roles', 'add run_agent_task handler + tool', 'remove egg_lib/cli.py and relocate gha_exec', 'remove run_claude and compose.py', 'remove run_interactive', 'update docs', 'update tests'. Each commit should be independently reviewable. Run `make test` locally before push to catch the mechanical failures early. Keep the doc update commit last so a reviewer reading the PR sees behavior changes before doc changes.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — review discipline and commit hygiene handle this.

risks.title: Docs drift — 8+ files still reference removed flags and paths after merge
risks.impact: Users following the docs hit errors; onboarding friction; loss of trust in docs as a source.
risks.description: Files known to reference removed behavior: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/guides/local-quickstart.md, docs/guides/deployment.md, docs/guides/deploy-migration.md, docs/architecture/kubernetes-migration.md, docs/reference/orchestrator-cli.md. The Makefile also references `egg --setup`. feedback-1 Q9 explicitly defers the doc rewrite list to this plan phase.

mitigation.strategy: The task_planner should enumerate each doc file with a specific acceptance criterion per file (e.g. 'local-quickstart.md: replace `egg --setup` with the new host-MCP workflow; strip all --compose/--public/--private references'). A dedicated 'doc sweep' task at the end of the implement phase with a grep-based acceptance criterion: `grep -rE '\begg --setup|\begg --reset|docker-compose|--public|--private|ensure_compose_services' README.md CONTRIBUTING.md CLAUDE.md docs/ Makefile` must return ZERO matches before merge. Historical docs like kubernetes-migration.md keep the compose → k8s table as a historical footnote.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — a grep-based gate makes this mechanically verifiable.

risks.title: HITL gate integration scope for run_agent_task is unresolved (feedback-1 Q1)
risks.impact: If CUSTOM pipelines skip HITL gates that other modes enforce (or vice versa), operators get inconsistent approval flows across modes.
risks.description: feedback-1 Q1 deferred HITL gate integration scope to plan phase. ISSUE pipelines pass through HITL decision gates at phase boundaries; BABYSIT does not (it's a single phase). CUSTOM with phase='refine' naturally triggers refine-phase HITL decisions; CUSTOM with phase='implement' on an existing PR might or might not. Unresolved behavior forces the coder to guess.

mitigation.strategy: The plan phase must explicitly resolve feedback-1 Q1. Recommended default: HITL decisions created during a CUSTOM phase are captured the same way as in ISSUE mode — i.e. any producer can call `egg-contract add-decision`, the orchestrator surfaces it to the operator, and phase completion waits for resolution the same way ISSUE does. The task_planner should make this an explicit task with tests.

risks.review_reason: feedback-1 Q1 was explicitly deferred; the plan phase is the correct place to resolve it.

rollback_plan.strategy: Option A is a single-PR cutover, so rollback is a single `git revert <merge_sha>` plus a sandbox image re-publish. The PR must pass CI on a squash-merge so the revert is a single commit. Rollback constraints: (a) any CUSTOM pipelines created post-merge would orphan on revert — state_store must fail loud rather than silent when it sees an unknown PipelineMode value; (b) the sandbox image published from the merge SHA contains the new gha_exec path — on revert, pin the GHA action to a pre-merge image tag until the reverted code re-publishes. Document both constraints in the PR description under 'rollback notes'.
signal_for_rollback: GHA failures across multiple consumer repositories on the new egg action release
Orchestrator fails to deserialize pipelines after restart (Pipeline model validation errors)
Any run_agent_task invocation hangs past the BRC timeout with no CONSENSUS_REACHED
monitoring: Post-merge: watch orchestrator structured logs for `pipeline.load.error` and `pipeline.mode.unknown` events.
Post-merge: watch GHA dashboards for action-level ImportError on the first 10 runs.
Add a metric / log line when run_agent_task is invoked and when it reaches CONSENSUS_REACHED — track the delta to catch hangs early.

areas_requiring_human_review.question: Is action/entrypoint.sh updated to import gha_exec from its new module in the same commit, and does the sandbox image COPY directive ship the new module?

Decision-6 resolves reviewer-only rosters but NOT producer-without-critical-reviewer rosters. Should run_agent_task (a) reject, or (b) auto-inject the critical reviewers — mirroring the reviewer_contract auto-include rule?

Every `mode == PipelineMode.BABYSIT` conditional in the codebase needs a policy call for CUSTOM. Should the plan enumerate each site (11+ in pipelines.py alone) or delegate the case-by-case call to the coder?
Does run_agent_task enforce the repositories.yaml allowlist at pipeline-creation time, identical to submit_task? This should be an explicit acceptance criterion in the plan.
When issue_number is provided to run_agent_task, should drafts be keyed by pipeline_id (avoid ISSUE collision) or by issue_number (shared with ISSUE)? feedback-1 Q2 explicitly defers this.
Does CUSTOM pipeline creation honor HITL decision gates the same way ISSUE does, or is phase completion non-blocking on unresolved decisions? feedback-1 Q1 explicitly defers this.

go_no_go.rationale: The architecture is sound and exploits existing primitives (ConcurrentPhaseExecutor roles override, ApprovalMatrix short-circuit, Pipeline mode enum). Every identified risk has a concrete mitigation that fits inside the Option A single-PR cutover. The six questions above should be resolved as task_planner acceptance criteria (and a few as plan-phase HITL decisions) before handoff to implement, but none of them block the plan phase itself.
conditions: Task planner enumerates the PipelineMode.BABYSIT audit (R5) as a discrete task with the full grep-identified list of sites as acceptance criteria.
Task planner resolves feedback-1 Q1 (HITL gates) and Q2 (draft-file keying) as explicit acceptance criteria, not deferred notes.
Task planner adds a run_agent_task security-allowlist test task (R9) with explicit pass/fail criteria.
Task planner adds a reviewer-graph validation task (R3) covering the producer-without-critical-reviewer case.
Task planner adds a 'doc sweep grep gate' task (R13) with a zero-match grep command as the acceptance criterion.
Task planner adds an integration_tests fixture migration task (R4) with k8s-prerequisite and clean-skip acceptance criteria.
